en: Dawn ran on a xenon-ion engine whose thrust you could have balanced on your palm — and rode that whisper for years, becoming the only craft ever to orbit two separate worlds beyond Earth: first Vesta, then Ceres.
cur: Dawn装备离子发动机，其推力可以在你的手掌上保持平衡——它靠着这一丝推力航行了多年，成为唯一在地球外两个独立天体周围轨道运行的航天器：先是灶神星，然后是谷神星。

en: Ion and Hall drives still carry propellant. They carry much less of it, and they use it far more efficiently, but the rocket equation still applies: the xenon runs out, and when it does, the thrust stops. The most radical escape from the equation is to carry no propellant at all — to push against something outside the spacecraft.
cur: 离子和霍尔驱动仍然携带推进剂。它们携带少得多的推进剂，使用效率远高，但火箭方程仍然适用：氙气耗尽，当它耗尽时，推力停止。最根本的逃离方程的方法是根本不携带推进剂——对航天器外的东西施加推力。

en: Photons carry momentum. Light pushes. The pressure is tiny — at Earth's distance from the Sun, sunlight exerts about nine micronewtons per square metre of illuminated surface — but it is free, inexhaustible, and it never runs out. A sail large enough and light enough will accelerate indefinitely as long as it faces the Sun, trading thrust for patience the way an ion engine does, but without a propellant budget at all.
cur: 光子携带动量。光可以推动。压力很小——在地球距离太阳处，阳光在被照亮表面每平方米施加约9微牛顿——但它是免费的、无穷无尽的，永远不会耗尽。足够大且足够轻的帆会无限加速，只要它面向太阳，就像离子发动机一样用推力换取耐心，但根本没有推进剂预算。

en: The idea is older than spaceflight by a century: Johannes Kepler noted in 1619 that comet tails always point away from the Sun and attributed it, correctly, to solar pressure. The mathematics were fully worked out by the 1920s. What was missing was a material: a sail light enough to matter, tough enough to survive the radiation environment of space, deployable from a rocket fairing. For most of the twentieth century it remained an idea.
cur: 这个想法比太空飞行早了一个世纪：约翰内斯·开普勒在1619年注意到彗星尾总是指向远离太阳的方向，并正确地将其归因于太阳压力。数学在1920年代已完全算出。缺少的是材料：一种足够轻能起作用的帆，足够耐硬足以存活太空辐射环境，能从火箭整流罩展开。整个二十世纪，它一直是一个想法。

en: JAXA flew the first one. On 21 May 2010, the Japanese spacecraft IKAROS — *Interplanetary Kite-craft Accelerating Radiation Of the Sun* — deployed a 200-square-metre polyimide sail en route to Venus and became the first spacecraft to achieve meaningful propulsion from sunlight alone in deep space. It measured the acceleration. It worked. The Planetary Society's LightSail 2, launched in 2019, went further: a small, shoebox-stacked CubeSat that deployed a 32-square-metre sail and became the first spacecraft to measurably raise its orbit using only the pressure of light. Both missions were small, low-budget, and largely ignored by the wider press. Between them they established that solar sailing is not a thought experiment.
cur: JAXA飞行了第一个。在2010年5月21日，日本航天器IKAROS——*Interplanetary Kite-craft Accelerating Radiation Of the 太阳*——在飞往金星的途中展开了200平方米的聚酰亚胺帆，成为第一艘在深空中仅从阳光获得有意义推进的航天器。它测量了加速度。成功了。行星协会的LightSail 2在2019年发射，更进一步：一颗小的、鞋盒堆放的CubeSat，展开32平方米的帆，成为第一艘仅使用光的压力可测量地提高其轨道的航天器。两项任务都规模较小、预算低廉、在更广泛的媒体中基本被忽视。但它们共同确立了太阳帆不是思想实验。

en: NASA's Advanced Composite Solar Sail System — ACS3 — launched in April 2024, carrying an 80-square-metre sail on composite boom arms stiffer and lighter than any previous design, demonstrating the structural technology needed to scale up. NEA Scout, which would have been the first solar sail to visit a near-Earth asteroid, launched aboard Artemis I in November 2022 and was lost — its radio never made contact after deployment, a reminder that small missions fly small margins. The setback did not cancel the program. The reason sails are worth pursuing is not the acceleration they give today but the acceleration they give tomorrow: a solar sail ten kilometres across, launched toward the inner solar system where sunlight is stronger, would reach speeds unattainable by any propellant-limited system. Sails are the only architecture for which *making the sail larger* makes the physics better, without adding propellant mass.
cur: NASA 的先进复合太阳帆系统 ACS3 于 2024 年 4 月发射，携带一张 80 平方米的帆，其复合式吊臂比任何先前的设计都更坚硬、更轻，展示了扩大规模所需的结构技术。NEA Scout 本应成为首个访问近地小行星的太阳帆，于 2022 年 11 月随 Artemis I 发射升空，随后丧失联系——其无线电在部署后从未建立过联系，这提醒我们小型任务的成功空间很小。这次失败并未使项目下马。太阳帆值得追求的原因不在于它们今天能提供的加速度，而在于它们明天能提供的加速度：一张宽度为十公里的太阳帆向太阳系内部发射，在那里阳光更强，将达到任何受推进剂限制的系统都无法达到的速度。帆是唯一一种架构，其中*扩大帆的尺寸*会改进物理学效果，而无需增加推进剂质量。

en: There is a third exit, and it is the one that, in the 1960s, seemed most likely to be first. A nuclear reactor running at high temperature can heat a propellant — hydrogen is the best choice, being the lightest gas and therefore fastest when expelled — and exhaust it through a nozzle. No combustion. No bond energies. The heat source is fission, and the temperatures a reactor can sustain are limited not by chemistry but by metallurgy: how hot can the fuel elements and the nozzle throat be made before they fail? The answer, in the engines tested at the Nevada Test Site from 1959 to 1969 under the program called NERVA, was hot enough to achieve specific impulses around 825 seconds — nearly twice the best chemical engine, at thrust levels measured in tens of kilonewtons, useful for a crewed Mars mission.
cur: 有第三条出路，在1960年代似乎最可能首先出现。高温运行的核反应堆可以加热推进剂——氢是最好的选择，因为它是最轻的气体，因此喷出时速度最快——并通过喷嘴排出。没有燃烧。没有键能。热源是裂变，反应堆能维持的温度受限不是化学，而是冶金学：在燃料元件和喷嘴喉部失效前能承受多高的温度？答案在1959年至1969年在内华达州核试验地点进行、名为NERVA的计划中测试的发动机中得到了回答，能达到比冲约825秒——接近最好化学发动机的两倍，推力水平在数十千牛顿，对载人火星任务有用。

en: The Phoebus 2A reactor, tested in 1968, was the most powerful nuclear rocket engine ever fired: 4,100 megawatts of thermal power, the equivalent of four large commercial nuclear power plants running simultaneously, all compressed into a structure the size of a car. The XE Prime engine, tested in 1969 in a configuration designed to simulate altitude firing, demonstrated restart capability and throttling — exactly the operational flexibility a crewed mission would need. The program accumulated more than two hours of total run time, including 28 minutes at full power. By every technical measure, it worked.
cur: Phoebus 2A反应堆在1968年测试，是有史以来最强大的核火箭发动机：热功率4,100兆瓦，相当于四个大型商业核电站同时运行，全部压缩在一个汽车大小的结构中。XE Prime发动机在1969年进行了测试，配置用于模拟高空发射，展示了重启能力和节流——正是载人任务所需的操作灵活性。该计划累积了两个多小时的总运行时间，包括28分钟满功率运行。按照每一项技术标准，它都有效。

en: And then it stopped. In 1973, with the Moon program over and budgets collapsing and no Mars mission forthcoming, NERVA was cancelled. The engines sat in Nevada. The knowledge spread into reports that aged in archives. For fifty years, no nuclear thermal rocket engine flew, or was seriously scheduled to fly. The [gravity assists](/science/transfers/gravity-assist) of [Voyager 2](/missions?id=voyager-2) made the outer planets reachable without nuclear propulsion. The outer planets were enough.
cur: 然后它停止了。在1973年，随着月球计划结束、预算崩溃、没有火星任务在望，NERVA被取消了。发动机留在内华达州。知识散布在随时间老化的档案报告中。五十年来，没有核热火箭发动机飞行，或被认真安排飞行。[Voyager 2](/missions?id=voyager-2)的[引力辅助](/science/transfers/gravity-assist)使外行星无需核推进就可到达。外行星足够了。

en: The idea came back slowly in the 2010s, and more urgently in the 2020s: a crewed mission to Mars, with a flight time measured in months rather than years, almost demands nuclear-thermal propulsion. DARPA's DRACO program — *Demonstration Rocket for Agile Cislunar Operations* — was the most concrete recent attempt to close the fifty-year gap, aiming to demonstrate a nuclear thermal engine in orbit. In June 2025, DARPA cancelled it. The official reasoning cited decreasing launch costs that diminished the economic case and infrastructure barriers around ground testing a nuclear reactor that had been underestimated at program start. The decision was not a technical verdict: no one tested the engine and found it wanting. The gap simply widened again.
cur: 想法在2010年代缓慢回归，在2020年代更为紧迫：一次载人火星任务，飞行时间以月而非年计，几乎需要核热推进。国防高级研究计划局(DARPA)的DRACO计划——*Demonstration Rocket for Agile Cislunar Operations(用于敏捷近地轨道操作的演示火箭)*——是最近弥合五十年差距的最具体尝试，目标是在轨道上演示核热发动机。在2025年6月，DARPA取消了它。官方理由引用了降低的发射成本，削弱了经济理由，以及围绕地面测试核反应堆的基础设施障碍，这些在计划开始时被低估了。这个决定不是技术判决：没有人测试发动机然后发现它不够好。差距简单地再次扩大了。

en: There is no flame here at all. A reactor heats hydrogen past any temperature a chemical fire can reach and throws it from the nozzle at roughly twice the speed — the same fuel, worth twice the push, and a shorter, less-irradiated road to Mars.
cur: 这里根本没有火焰。反应堆将氢加热到超过任何化学火焰所能达到的温度，并从喷嘴以大约两倍的速度喷出——同样的燃料，值得两倍的推动力，通往火星的道路更短、辐射更少。

en: The history of advanced propulsion is not, mostly, a history of technical failure. Ion drives work; every deep-space spacecraft that has carried one has performed as predicted. Solar sails work; IKAROS measured the thrust, LightSail 2 changed its orbit. Nuclear-thermal engines worked; NERVA demonstrated it in six decades of un-revisited ground tests. The failures are almost entirely in the space between a working technology and a funded mission.
cur: 高级推进的历史在大多数情况下不是技术失败的历史。离子驱动有效；每一艘携带过它们的深空航天器都按预期表现。太阳帆有效；IKAROS测量了推力，LightSail 2改变了轨道。核热发动机有效；NERVA在六十年未被重新审视的地面测试中证明了这一点。失败几乎完全在工作技术和融资任务之间的空间中。

en: Part of it is the nature of these drives. Chemical rockets are violent and obvious — they shake the ground and light the sky and deliver their result in minutes. Ion and Hall thrusters produce a force you cannot feel, run for years before the result becomes visible, and require patience from funders who face budget cycles measured in months. Solar sails require large, delicate structures that complicate launch packaging. Nuclear-thermal engines require a reactor, and a reactor in space has a regulatory complexity that adds years and uncertainty to any program before the first component is machined. None of these are fundamental barriers. They are, in the language of systems engineering, *not-yet-solved integration problems* — and integration problems get solved when there is enough pressure behind them.
cur: 部分是这些驱动的性质。化学火箭是暴力而明显的——它们震撼地面、照亮天空、在几分钟内交付结果。离子和霍尔推进器产生你感受不到的力，运行数年后结果才变得可见，需要面临以月为周期预算的资助者的耐心。太阳帆需要复杂发射包装的大型脆弱结构。核热发动机需要反应堆，轨道上的反应堆具有监管复杂性，在加工第一个部件之前就会给任何计划添加数年的不确定性。这些都不是根本障碍。用系统工程语言，它们是*尚未解决的整合问题*——整合问题在背后有足够压力时会得到解决。

en: The pressure is building. The [Tsiolkovsky rocket equation](/science/propulsion/tsiolkovsky) has not changed. A crewed Mars round-trip at chemical Isp is not impossible — it is just enormously expensive in propellant, and therefore in launch mass, and therefore in launch cost, and therefore in political will. As the cost per kilogram to orbit drops and the ambition of missions rises, the gap between what chemistry can do and what the mission demands grows wider. Every new target — the ice giants, an asteroid on a short timeline, Mars on a crewed flight that does not require pre-positioning years of propellant — presses against the ceiling a little harder.
cur: 压力在积累。[齐奥尔科夫斯基火箭方程](/science/propulsion/tsiolkovsky)没有改变。化学比冲的载人火星往返不是不可能——只是推进剂极其昂贵，因此发射质量昂贵，因此发射成本昂贵，因此政治意愿有限。随着轨道成本每公斤下降、任务野心上升，化学能做到的和任务要求的之间的差距越来越大。每个新目标——冰巨星、短时间表上的小行星、不需要多年提前配置推进剂的载人飞行火星——都对天花板施加了更大的压力。

en: What is strange, surveying this history, is not that the alternatives haven't flown — it is that they have been ready, in principle, for so long. The specific impulse limits of nuclear-thermal propulsion were calculated before Sputnik. The physics of solar sailing were understood before the Second World War. The concept of ion propulsion appeared in an Esther Goddard memoir describing a conversation with Robert Goddard in 1906, four years before he flew anything. The ideas are old. The flying is new.
cur: 奇怪的是，审视这段历史时，不是这些替代品未曾飞行——而是它们在原则上已准备就绪这么久。核热推进的比冲极限在Sputnik发射前就已被计算。太阳帆的物理学在第二次世界大战前就被理解。离子推进的概念出现在Esther Goddard的回忆录中，描述了她与罗伯特·戈达德在1906年的一次对话，早于他飞行任何东西四年。想法是旧的。飞行是新的。

en: What [Dawn](/missions?id=dawn) established is the practical benchmark: ion propulsion is not exotic. It is the correct choice for any mission that requires multiple destinations, large velocity changes, or flight times long enough for continuous thrust to accumulate. The missions that come after Psyche — robotic science probes to the ice giants, fast-transit cargo to a lunar Gateway, prospectors at the inner asteroid belt — are the natural clients. Hall thrusters at [Psyche's](/missions?id=psyche) scale will be routine within a decade because the economics already work.
cur: [Dawn](/missions?id=dawn)建立的是实践基准：离子推进不是奇异的。对于任何需要多个目的地、大的速度变化或足够长飞行时间以使连续推力积累的任务，它是正确的选择。Psyche之后的任务——对冰巨星的机器人科学探针、到月球Gateway的快速运输货物、内小行星带的勘探者——是自然的客户。[Psyche](/missions?id=psyche)规模的Hall推进器将在十年内成为常规，因为经济学已经可行。

en: Solar sailing is further from routine, but the trajectory is clear: each generation of sail is larger, the booms lighter, the control systems more sophisticated. The physics reward scale in a way no other propulsion mode does. A sail the size of a sports stadium, with a spacecraft bus the mass of a desk, accelerated by a laser from the inner solar system rather than by ambient sunlight — this is the architecture proposed for interstellar precursor missions, reaching speeds of hundreds of kilometres per second. The sail does not care about the rocket equation. It has no propellant to run out of.
cur: 太阳帆离常规更远，但轨迹很清晰：每一代帆都更大，撑杆更轻，控制系统更复杂。物理学奖励以其他推进模式都没有的方式扩展。一张体育场大小的帆，航天器总线质量如办公桌，由来自内太阳系而非周围阳光的激光加速——这是为行星际先驱任务提出的架构，达到数百公里每秒的速度。帆不关心火箭方程。它没有推进剂可耗尽。

en: Nuclear-thermal propulsion is the hardest call. DRACO's cancellation in 2025 closed the most concrete near-term path. But the technical case — 825 seconds of specific impulse at high thrust, the only combination of efficiency and power that opens a fast crewed Mars transit — has not weakened. The knowledge from NERVA was not lost; it was archived. What is missing is not the engineering. It is a program with enough longevity to navigate the regulatory and infrastructure work that the 1960s began but never finished. If a crewed Mars mission becomes a fixed political objective rather than a recurring aspiration, nuclear-thermal propulsion will almost certainly be part of how it is done. The engines work. They are waiting.
cur: 核热推进是最难的决定。DRACO在2025年的取消关闭了最具体的近期路径。但技术论据——825秒比冲加上高推力，是唯一结合效率和功率打开快速载人火星运输的组合——没有被削弱。NERVA的知识没有丢失；它被存档了。缺少的不是工程。而是具有足够寿命的计划，以应对1960年代开始但从未完成的监管和基础设施工作。如果载人火星任务成为一个固定的政治目标，而不是一个反复出现的愿望，核热推进几乎肯定会成为实现方式的一部分。发动机有效。它们在等待。

en: The chemical rocket did extraordinary things. It carried twelve people to the surface of the Moon. It landed a car-sized rover on Mars at the end of seven minutes of automated terror. It put the James Webb Space Telescope in its L2 halo orbit with so little error that the fuel margin for station-keeping, originally budgeted for ten years, now projects to last twenty. For getting mass off Earth's surface against gravity — the hardest part of any space mission — it will remain the tool for the foreseeable future. The Tsiolkovsky equation punishes propellant mass in orbit less than it does on the ground, and no ion thruster will lift anything from a launch pad.
cur: 化学火箭做了非凡的事情。它把十二个人送到了月球表面。它在七分钟自动恐怖的末尾登陆了一辆汽车大小的火星漫游车。它在站点保持燃料的误差如此之小下将James Webb Space Telescope放在其L2晕轮轨道上，原本预算十年的燃料储备现在预计能持续二十年。对于将质量从地球表面对抗重力——任何太空任务最难的部分——提升，它在可预见的未来将保持工具。Tsiolkovsky方程对轨道上的推进剂质量的惩罚比地面上的更少，没有离子推进器会从发射台提升任何东西。

en: But the ceiling above low Earth orbit is chemistry's ceiling, and the solar system above it is chemistry's trap. The exits have been drawn on the map for a hundred years. Ion drives are already flying. Sails have already changed orbits. The nuclear option is on hold, not on the shelf. We have known how to leave the chemical era since before the chemical era's greatest triumphs. We are, slowly, learning to mean it.
cur: 但低地球轨道上的天花板是化学的天花板，其上的太阳系是化学的陷阱。出口已经在地图上绘制了一百年。离子驱动已在飞行。帆已改变轨道。核选项在暂停中，不在架子上。我们从化学时代最伟大的胜利之前就知道如何离开化学时代。我们正慢慢学会认真对待它。

en: Line the exits up by efficiency and the pattern is plain: every road out of the chemical era trades brute thrust for the patience to keep pushing. All of them were sketched on paper before the first satellite ever flew.
cur: 按效率排列出口，模式很清晰：离开化学时代的每条路都用蛮力换取继续推动的耐心。所有这些都在第一颗卫星升空前就被勾勒在纸上。

en: For sixty years we built the most expensive machine in human history, flew it once, and dropped it in the ocean. The people who decided to stop doing that have quietly pulled off the biggest shift in spaceflight since Apollo.
cur: 六十年来，我们建造了人类历史上最昂贵的机器，飞行一次，然后将其丢入海洋。决定停止这样做的人们悄悄地完成了自Apollo任务以来太空飞行中最大的转变。

en: On the night of 21 December 2015, a [Falcon 9](/fleet?id=falcon-9) first stage stood vertically on a concrete pad at Cape Canaveral, engines cold, surrounded by a cloud of residual vapour, intact. It had just come back from space. About eight minutes after lifting off to deliver a batch of satellites to orbit, the booster had flipped itself around, relit three of its nine Merlin engines, braked through the upper atmosphere, deployed four landing legs, and set itself down upright on the pad it had left. The whole manoeuvre took the kind of precision usually reserved for a Swiss watch. The crowd watching erupted, and the sound — a roar of people who had just watched something genuinely new — is still in the video.
cur: 在2015年12月21日夜间，一枚[Falcon 9](/fleet?id=falcon-9)第一级火箭在卡纳维拉尔角的混凝土发射台上竖直站立，引擎冷却，被残留蒸汽云包围，完好无损。它刚刚从太空返回。在起飞约八分钟后将一批卫星送入轨道后，助推器自己翻转过来，重新点燃了九台Merlin引擎中的三台，通过上层大气制动，展开四条着陆腿，然后直立地落在它离开的发射台上。整个机动所需的精度通常仅限于瑞士手表。观看的人群欢呼雀跃，那声音——人们刚刚目睹真正新奇事物时的欢呼声——仍然在视频中回荡。

en: What happened that night was a demonstration, but what it demonstrated was not primarily a technical trick. It was an economic argument. Every rocket ever flown before it — the [Saturn V](/fleet?id=saturn-v) that sent twelve people to the Moon, the Soviet N1 that never made it to orbit, the workhorse Soyuz and Atlas and Proton and Long March families that between them account for most of the launches in this atlas — was built to be used once. You flew it. It fell apart in the atmosphere or sank in the sea. You built another one. The industry had been structured around this fact for sixty years: rockets were ammunition, not aircraft. The moment that Falcon 9 landed, that assumption was on the table for the first time.
cur: 那晚发生的事是一场演示，但它演示的主要不是技术技巧。这是一个经济学论证。在它之前飞过的每一枚火箭——将12个人送上月球的[Saturn V](/fleet?id=saturn-v)、从未进入轨道的苏联N1，以及辛劳的Soyuz、Atlas、Proton和长征系列火箭，它们合起来占了本图集中大多数发射的份额——都是为了只用一次而制造的。你发射它。它在大气中散裂或沉入大海。你制造另一枚。六十年来，整个工业都是围绕这个事实组织的：火箭是弹药，不是飞机。Falcon 9着陆的那一刻，这个假设第一次被提出质疑。

en: Why it had taken sixty years to get there is a more interesting question than it looks.
cur: 为什么花了六十年才到达这里是一个比它看起来更有趣的问题。

en: The expendable rocket is wasteful in a way that is almost comical when you describe it plainly. A [Saturn V](/fleet?id=saturn-v) cost something in the range of $185 million in late-1960s dollars — roughly $1.5 billion at today's prices — and each one flew for about twelve minutes before being discarded. The five F-1 engines in its first stage, each one a staggering piece of machinery that burned roughly 2,600 kilograms of propellant per second, ended their lives rusting on the floor of the Atlantic. A private expedition funded by Jeff Bezos recovered two sets of Saturn V F-1 engines from the seafloor in 2013, nearly half a century after they were dropped there, and found them largely intact. They went to museums, not back to flight. Throwing them away the first time was the plan.
cur: 一次性火箭的浪费方式几乎是荒唐可笑的，当你直白地描述它的时候。一枚[Saturn V](/fleet?id=saturn-v)花费大约1.85亿美元（1960年代末的价格）——按今天的价格来算大约15亿美元——每一枚飞行约12分钟后就被弃用了。它第一级的五台F-1引擎，每一台都是令人瞩目的机器，每秒钟燃烧约2600公斤推进剂，最后的下场是在大西洋海底生锈。由杰夫·贝索斯资助的一支私人远征队在2013年从海底打捞回了两套Saturn V F-1引擎，距离它们被丢弃那里已经近半个世纪，并发现它们基本上完好无损。它们进了博物馆，而没有重新飞行。第一次就把它们扔掉是计划中的事。

en: The logic behind this plan was not stupidity. It was the logic of the 1960s Space Race: get there first, at whatever cost. Building a reusable rocket is harder than building an expendable one. Reusability adds weight — heat shields, landing legs, propellant reserved for the return burn — and weight is the enemy, because every kilogram you add to the structure is a kilogram you cannot deliver to orbit. Early designers ran the numbers and concluded that the penalty was too steep. Better, they decided, to build cheap and throw away. That calculation was right for its moment, and it locked in a set of assumptions that lasted two generations.
cur: 这项计划背后的逻辑不是愚蠢。这是20世纪60年代太空竞赛的逻辑：无论成本如何都要首先到达。建造可重复使用的火箭比建造一次性火箭更难。可重复使用增加了重量——隔热盾、着陆腿、为返回燃烧保留的推进剂——而重量是敌人，因为你添加到结构中的每一千克都是你无法送入轨道的一千克。早期设计师进行了计算，得出惩罚太陡的结论。他们决定，更好的办法是建造便宜且可丢弃的。这种计算对当时是正确的，它锁定了持续两代人的一系列假设。

en: The [Space Shuttle](/fleet?id=space-shuttle-stack) was supposed to break the logic. It was the first genuine attempt by the United States — or anyone — to build an operationally reusable launch system, and the argument for it was economic: by flying the orbiter repeatedly, the program would drive the cost of reaching orbit down toward $600 per kilogram, low enough to make spaceflight almost routine. The shuttle flew 135 missions between 1981 and 2011. It failed the economic test completely. The real cost per flight averaged around $1.5 billion when total program expenses were spread across all missions — more expensive per kilogram to low Earth orbit than the Saturn V it replaced. Refurbishing the orbiter's 24,000 heat-shield tiles after each flight was not a quick job; it ate thousands of person-hours. Reuse turned out to be extraordinarily expensive when every subsystem had to be torn down and rebuilt to the standards of an aircraft that might carry crew. The shuttle proved that reusability *could* work mechanically — the orbiter flew dozens of times — but it also proved that reusability by itself does not reduce costs. The economics only work if you can turn the vehicle around *fast* and *cheaply*.
cur: [Space Shuttle](/fleet?id=space-shuttle-stack)本应打破这一逻辑。这是美国第一次——或任何人——真正尝试建造可操作重复使用发射系统，其论据是经济学：通过重复飞行轨道舱，该项目将把到达轨道的成本驱动到每千克600美元左右，低到足以使太空飞行几乎成为常规。航天飞机在1981年至2011年间飞行了135次任务。它完全没有通过经济测试。当总项目支出分散在所有任务中时，实际每次飞行平均成本约为15亿美元——按千克计算到近地轨道比它取代的土星五号更昂贵。在每次飞行后翻新轨道舱的24,000块隔热瓦片不是快速的工作；它耗费了数千人小时。当每个子系统都必须拆卸并重建以达到可能携带船员的飞机标准时，重复使用证明成本极其高昂。航天飞机证明了可重复使用在机械上*可以*工作——轨道舱飞行了数十次——但它也证明了可重复使用本身并不能降低成本。经济只有在你可以*快速*和*廉价*地周转车辆时才有效。

en: SpaceX approached the problem differently. Rather than trying to reuse the whole vehicle — the choice that made the Shuttle so complex — the company focused on the most expensive single component: the first-stage booster. In a typical rocket, the first stage does the heaviest lifting, burning the most propellant, carrying the most engine mass, and costing the most to manufacture. It is also the component that, on an expendable rocket, you lose every time. Save the first stage, and you have recovered the majority of the vehicle's value.
cur: SpaceX以不同的方式接近这个问题。与其尝试重复使用整个车辆——这个选择使Shuttle变得如此复杂——该公司将重点放在最昂贵的单一组件：第一级助推器。在典型火箭中，第一级进行最重的举升，燃烧最多推进剂，携带最多引擎质量，制造成本最高。这也是在一次性火箭上你每次都会失去的组件。保存第一级，你已经恢复了车辆价值的大部分。

en: The technical requirement for saving it is brutal: the stage has to survive reentry through an atmosphere it spent the first few minutes punching through at Mach 7, reverse direction, slow from hypersonic to landing speed, and set down vertically on a target the size of a football field — either back at the launch site or on a drone ship hundreds of kilometres downrange in the Atlantic or Pacific. To accomplish all of this, the booster has to retain enough propellant for a series of precisely timed engine relights, which means it arrives in orbit with less fuel for the main job. That weight penalty is real: a Falcon 9 flying with a new booster delivers about 22,800 kilograms to low Earth orbit; a flight that recovers the booster delivers less. This is the fundamental trade at the heart of reusable launch, and SpaceX accepted it because the economics work regardless: the booster that lands can fly again, and again, and again.
cur: 保存它的技术要求是残酷的：该级必须存活重返穿过它在前几分钟以Mach 7速度穿过的大气，反向方向，从高超音速减速到着陆速度，并竖直落在足球场大小的目标上——无论是返回发射场还是在大西洋或太平洋远处数百千米的无人船上。为了完成所有这些，助推器必须保留足够的推进剂用于一系列精确定时的引擎重新点火，这意味着它到达轨道时燃料较少以完成主要任务。这个重量惩罚是真实的：配备新助推器飞行的Falcon 9向近地轨道运送约22,800千克；恢复助推器的飞行运送较少。这是可重复使用发射心脏的基本权衡，SpaceX接受了它，因为不管怎样经济都有效：着陆的助推器可以再次飞行，一次又一次。

en: After the December 2015 landing came a second, and a third, and then the reflight: in March 2017, SpaceX launched a Falcon 9 on a booster that had already flown, the first time in history that an orbital-class rocket stage flew to space twice. By mid-2026, the most-flown Falcon 9 first stage has completed 33 missions on the same hardware — more than most expendable rockets fly in total across an entire fleet. The marginal cost of a reused launch, with propellant and refurbishment, sits around $15 to $20 million against a list price of $74 million. The difference, roughly, is the cost of the booster itself, recovered by recovery.
cur: 2015年12月着陆之后，又有第二次、第三次，随后是复飞：2017年3月，SpaceX用已经执行过一次任务的助推器发射了一枚Falcon 9火箭，这是历史上首次轨道级火箭助推级飞向太空两次。到2026年中期，飞行次数最多的Falcon 9一级火箭已在同一硬件上完成了33次任务——超过大多数消耗性火箭在整个舰队中终身飞行的次数。一次复用发射的边际成本，包括推进剂和翻新，约为1500万至2000万美元，而官方价格为7400万美元。其中的差价，大致上就是助推器本身的成本，通过回收得以收回。

en: The trick is almost insultingly simple to state and brutal to fly: hold back enough propellant, flip the booster around, and burn three times on the way down — boostback, entry, landing — until it settles onto its legs. The same stage is then inspected, refuelled, and flown again.
cur: 这个技巧是陈述起来几乎令人讨厌的简单，但飞行却非常残酷：保留足够的推进剂，翻转助推器，并在下降过程中燃烧三次——助推返回、重返、着陆——直到它落在腿上。然后检查同一级，重新加油，再次飞行。

en: The [Falcon Heavy](/fleet?id=falcon-heavy) extended the same logic sideways: three Falcon 9 cores strapped together, two of them peeling off after the first two minutes and flying back to land simultaneously, side by side, at Cape Canaveral. The videos of the twin landings — two pillars of fire descending in mirror symmetry, touching down at the exact same instant — look like something from a film. They are not. They are the economics made visible.
cur: [Falcon Heavy](/fleet?id=falcon-heavy)以横向扩展了相同的逻辑：三个Falcon 9芯级绑在一起，其中两个在前两分钟后剥离并飞回同时在卡纳维拉尔角肩并肩着陆。双着陆的视频——两道火焰柱以镜像对称性下降，在完全相同的瞬间着陆——看起来像电影中的东西。它们不是。它们是经济学变得可见。

en: [Starship](/fleet?id=starship) takes the argument to its logical end. Where Falcon 9 recovers its first stage and disposes of its upper stage, Starship is designed to recover *both*. The Super Heavy booster — 71 metres tall, powered by 33 Raptor engines burning liquid methane and liquid oxygen, producing roughly twice the thrust of a Saturn V — returns to the launch site and is caught in mid-air by a pair of mechanical arms on the launch tower itself. The system is called Mechazilla by the engineers who built it. SpaceX first caught the booster this way on 13 October 2024, Flight 5 of the Starship test programme, and has repeated the manoeuvre on subsequent flights. The idea that you would not land your rocket but simply *catch it as it fell* would have sounded like fiction a decade ago. It is a Monday-morning procedure now.
cur: [Starship](/fleet?id=starship)将论证推向其逻辑终点。当Falcon 9恢复其第一级并处置其上级时，Starship被设计为恢复*两者*。Super Heavy助推器——71米高，由33台Raptor引擎驱动，燃烧液态甲烷和液态氧，产生大约土星五号推力的两倍——返回发射场，并在发射塔本身的一对机械臂中途被接住。该系统由建造它的工程师称为Mechazilla。SpaceX在2024年10月13日首次以这种方式接住了助推器，这是Starship测试计划的第5次飞行，并在随后的飞行中重复了这个机动。你不会着陆你的火箭而是简单地*在它下降时接住它*的想法十年前听起来会像虚构。现在这是一个星期一早上的常规程序。

en: The Starship upper stage — the largest spacecraft ever built, tall as a fifteen-storey building — is intended to follow the same path, returning and being caught above the pad. Once both halves are on the ground, the system can theoretically be refuelled and relaunched within hours. No expendable rocket even attempts this comparison. An expendable rocket is a logistics chain: manufacture, transport, integrate, launch, repeat from the start. A fully reusable system is an *aircraft* with a very long route. The economics of the two are not in the same galaxy.
cur: Starship上级——有史以来最大的航天器，高如十五层楼——旨在遵循相同的路径，返回并在垫台上方被接住。一旦两个半部分在地面上，系统在理论上可以在几小时内重新加油并重新发射。没有一枚可重复使用火箭甚至尝试这个比较。一枚可重复使用火箭是一条后勤链：制造、运输、整合、发射、从头开始重复。一个完全可重复使用系统是一架*飞机*，拥有非常长的路线。两者的经济学不在同一个星系。

en: Then a stranger idea: don’t give the booster legs at all. Let the launch tower catch it — two arms closing on a seventy-metre stage as it hovers, so the mass that would have been landing gear becomes payload instead. The first clean catch came in October 2024.
cur: 然后一个陌生的想法：根本不要给助推器腿。让发射塔接住它——两只手臂在七十米级悬停时闭合，使本应是着陆齿轮的质量变成有效载荷。第一次干净的捕捉来自2024年10月。

en: Blue Origin's [New Glenn](/fleet?id=new-glenn) landed its first stage at sea for the first time on 13 November 2025 — ten years after the December 2015 Falcon 9 landing, which gives a sense of how fast the industry moves when SpaceX is setting the pace. New Glenn is a large rocket by any previous standard, carrying up to 45,000 kilograms to low Earth orbit in expendable configuration; its first stage returns to a drone ship in the Atlantic on every mission. The first reuse of a New Glenn stage followed in April 2026. Blue Origin's approach mirrors SpaceX's in architecture: save the first stage, fly it again, cut the marginal cost with each reuse.
cur: Blue Origin的[New Glenn](/fleet?id=new-glenn)在2025年11月13日首次在海上着陆其第一级——距离2015年12月Falcon 9着陆十年，这样可以让人感受到当SpaceX设定步伐时这个行业的发展速度。New Glenn按任何以前的标准都是一枚大火箭，在可重复使用配置中可向近地轨道运送多达45,000千克；其第一级在每次任务中都返回大西洋的无人船。New Glenn级的首次重复使用随后在2026年4月进行。Blue Origin的方法在架构上反映了SpaceX的：保存第一级，再次飞行它，通过每次重复使用来削减边际成本。

en: What the emergence of [New Glenn](/fleet?id=new-glenn) adds to the picture is competitive pressure. For most of the decade between 2015 and 2025, SpaceX was essentially alone in the reusable-launch market. A market with one supplier is not a market; it's a monopoly. The entry of a second credible reusable launcher changes the pricing dynamics for everyone who buys a ride to orbit. Satellite operators, space agencies, and commercial customers who once had no choice but to take whatever SpaceX offered now have alternatives — and more are coming.
cur: [New Glenn](/fleet?id=new-glenn)的出现为图景增加的是竞争压力。在2015年至2025年间的大部分时间里，SpaceX基本上在可重复使用发射市场上孤军奋战。一个只有一个供应商的市场不是市场；那是垄断。第二个可信赖的可重复使用发射器的进入改变了为所有购买进入轨道航程的人的定价动态。卫星运营商、航天机构和商业客户，他们曾经别无选择只能接受SpaceX提供的任何东西，现在有替代品——更多的即将到来。

en: China has moved with unusual seriousness. LandSpace's Zhuque-3, a methane-fuelled rocket broadly analogous to Falcon 9, attempted its first recovery in December 2025; the upper stage reached orbit but the booster crashed on its landing approach. A second recovery attempt is planned for mid-2026. iSpace has its Hyperbola-3 in hardware qualification, with a dedicated drone ship already launched, and is targeting its first flight from Wenchang. Several other Chinese commercial companies are in active development. The Chinese government has made reusable access to orbit an explicit national priority. That the country that built the Great Wall has decided to stop throwing its rockets away is a data point worth sitting with.
cur: 中国以异常严肃的态度向前推进。LandSpace的朱雀三号，一枚甲烷燃料火箭，大致类似于Falcon 9，在2025年12月尝试了第一次回收；上级到达了轨道，但助推器在着陆方式上坠毁。第二次回收尝试计划在2026年年中进行。iSpace的Hyperbola-3在硬件鉴定中，专用无人船已经发射，并以文昌为目标进行首次飞行。其他几家中国商业公司正在积极开发中。中国政府已将可重复使用的轨道进入权设为明确的国家优先事项。建造了长城的国家决定停止扔掉它的火箭是一个值得思考的数据点。

en: A Falcon 9 first stage stands back on its legs after delivering a payload to orbit — the moment a sixty-year assumption quietly collapsed. Once one company proved a booster could be flown again, everyone else had to learn to keep theirs too.
cur: 猎鹰9号第一级在传送有效载荷到轨道后重新站在它的腿上——六十年假设悄悄崩塌的时刻。一旦一家公司证明了助推器可以再次飞行，其他所有人都必须学会保留他们的。

en: The surface story is cost reduction, and the cost reduction is real: launch prices that once sat at $200 million or more for a large expendable have fallen toward $60–$80 million for a reusable medium-lift mission, and the marginal economics of a well-worn Falcon 9 booster are lower still. But the deeper change is in launch *cadence*. SpaceX launched 132 Falcon 9 missions in 2024 — almost three per week, sustained across a full calendar year, with the same pool of boosters cycling through the pad and back again. No expendable architecture could approach that tempo; you would need an industrial supply chain operating at wartime pace to match it. Reusability, it turns out, is not just about cost. It is about rate. And rate is about what becomes possible.
cur: 表面故事是成本降低，成本降低是真实的：一次性大型火箭的发射价格曾经坐在2亿美元或更高，已经下降到可重复使用中型升力任务的6000至8000万美元，而一个磨损的Falcon 9助推器的边际经济学更低。但更深层的改变是在发射*频率*中。SpaceX在2024年发射了132次Falcon 9任务——几乎每周三次，全年持续，使用同一批助推器在垫台和返回中循环。没有可重复使用的架构可以接近这个速度；你需要一个工业供应链以战时节奏运作来匹配它。可重复使用，事实证明，不仅仅是关于成本。这是关于速率。而速率是关于什么变得可能。

en: What becomes possible is Starlink: a constellation that required more than 6,000 launches to populate, impossible to build under any expendable pricing structure that has ever existed. What becomes possible are low-cost commercial science missions that previously could not afford the ride. What becomes possible, eventually, is crewed transport to Mars at a frequency that makes it a programme rather than a stunt — because the [delta-v budget](/science/propulsion/dv-budget) of an Earth-to-Mars mission demands a vehicle that can be refuelled on orbit and reused, or the mass fractions simply don't close. Reusability is not just an economic preference. For the ambitions that [Starship](/fleet?id=starship) is being designed to support, it is a physical requirement.
cur: 什么变得可能是Starlink：一个星座需要超过6,000次发射来填充，在任何有史以来存在的可重复使用定价结构下都无法建造。什么变得可能是低成本商业科学任务，以前买不起这种坐骑。什么变得可能，最终，是以一个使其成为计划而不是特技的频率来进行有人运输到火星——因为[地球对火星任务的delta-v预算](/science/propulsion/dv-budget)要求一个可以在轨道上重新加油并重复使用的车辆，否则质量分数就不会闭合。可重复使用不仅仅是经济偏好。对于[Starship](/fleet?id=starship)被设计来支持的雄心，这是一个物理要求。

en: The weight penalty that made early engineers dismiss reuse is still real; it has not been engineered away. A fully expendable Starship would deliver more to orbit than a reusable one. But the question is no longer whether you can afford the mass penalty. It's whether you can afford to throw the whole thing away — whether you can afford, as the rocket industry did for six decades, to treat the most complex machine ever built as a single-use item.
cur: 使早期工程师驳斥重复使用的重量惩罚仍然是真实的；它尚未被工程化消除。完全可重复使用的Starship会比可重复使用的交付更多到轨道。但问题不再是你是否能承担重量惩罚。这是你是否能承受扔掉整个东西——你是否能承受，就像火箭行业在六十年来所做的那样，将最复杂的机器视为一次性物品。

en: The number that gates everything is the price of a kilogram to orbit. The Shuttle promised to lower it and never did; reusable Falcon 9 cut it roughly twenty-fold. Drop it far enough and missions that were once unthinkable become merely scheduled.
cur: 门控一切的数字是每千克到轨道的价格。Shuttle承诺降低它但没有；可重复使用Falcon 9粗略地削减了二十倍。足够远地降低它，曾经不可想象的任务变成仅仅是安排的。

en: The rocket industry's original argument against reuse was engineering: the vehicle is too complex to refurbish cheaply, too fragile to fly again without dismantling, too weight-constrained to carry the hardware needed to land. The Space Shuttle's experience seemed to confirm all three. Those concerns were legitimate, and for thirty years they held.
cur: 火箭行业反对重复使用的原始论证是工程学：车辆太复杂而无法廉价翻新，太脆弱而无法在不拆卸的情况下再次飞行，重量约束太多而无法携带着陆所需的硬件。Space Shuttle的经历似乎证实了所有三点。这些顾虑是合理的，三十年来它们持续了。

en: What changed was not the physics. What changed was the manufacturing base, the propellant choice — methane burns cleaner than kerosene, leaves less residue, makes refurbishment faster — and, more than anything, the willingness to design for reuse from the start rather than retrofitting it onto a vehicle optimised for expendability. The Shuttle was an expendable rocket that had been told to come home. The Falcon 9 booster was designed from the beginning around the question of how to land. That difference in design intent accounts for most of the difference in outcome.
cur: 改变的不是物理学。改变的是制造基础、推进剂选择——甲烷燃烧更清洁比煤油，留下较少残留物，使翻新更快——而且，比什么都重要的是，从一开始就为重复使用设计而不是改装它到针对一次性进行优化的车辆的意愿。Shuttle是一枚被告知要回家的可重复使用火箭。Falcon 9助推器是从一开始就围绕如何着陆的问题设计的。这种设计意图的差异占了结果差异的大部分。

en: In the decade since that December night at Cape Canaveral, landing a booster has gone from impossible to ordinary. A Falcon 9 first stage that fails to return to its drone ship is now the unusual event, worth noting in the anomaly log. Super Heavy has been caught from the air. A second company has landed a heavy-lift stage at sea and flown it again. China is running to catch up. The assumption that has governed the entire launch industry since Sputnik — that a rocket is an expendable — has been broken, and the breaking of it is already reshaping which missions are possible, which businesses are viable, and what it will cost the next generation to go further.
cur: 在卡纳维拉尔角那个12月夜晚的十年里，着陆一个助推器已经从不可能变成了常规。一个Falcon 9第一级如果不能返回其无人船现在是不寻常的事件，值得在异常日志中记录。Super Heavy已从空中被接住。第二家公司已在海上着陆了重型升力级并再次飞行。中国正在加紧追上。自从Sputnik以来一直统治整个发射行业的假设——火箭是可重复使用的——已被打破，它的打破已经在重新塑造哪些任务是可能的，哪些业务是可行的，以及下一代走得更远需要花费多少。

en: None of the [rocket stages](/science/propulsion/rocket-stages) that ever took humans or spacecraft to orbit in the first sixty years of spaceflight survived. They are on the ocean floor, or in the upper atmosphere as dispersed molecules, or in museums where engineers who built them can walk past and recognise things they once touched. The ones flying now come back. That one change — quiet, technical, brutally difficult to make work — is the thing that separates the first era of spaceflight from whatever comes next.
cur: 在太空飞行的前六十年中，曾经将人类或航天器送入轨道的所有[火箭级](/science/propulsion/rocket-stages)都没有幸存。它们在海洋底部，或在上层大气中作为分散分子，或在博物馆里，建造它们的工程师可以走过并认出他们曾经接触过的东西。现在飞行的那些回来。那一个改变——安静、技术、残酷地难以工作——是将太空飞行的第一个纪元与接下来的任何东西分开的东西。

en: Starship is the larger wager: that the whole vehicle — booster and ship alike — comes home and flies again within days. If it holds, the cost of reaching orbit stops being the thing that decides what humanity is allowed to attempt.
cur: Starship 是更大的赌注：整个车辆——助推器和飞船一样——回家并在数日内再次飞行。如果它持有，到达轨道的成本停止成为决定人类被允许尝试的东西。

en: The cruise is easy. You spend months doing almost nothing — coasting on physics, nudging a trajectory, waiting. Arriving is where missions die. Landing is the hardest thing in spaceflight, and we have never solved it the same way twice.
cur: 巡航很容易。你花几个月的时间几乎什么都不做——靠物理学惯性滑行，微调轨迹，等待。抵达才是任务的死亡之地。着陆是航天飞行中最困难的事，而我们从未用同一种方式解决过两次。

en: Consider what the number means. Seven minutes: from the first bite of atmosphere at roughly 20,000 kilometres per hour to wheels-down, stationary, on another planet. Seven minutes in which a spacecraft that cost a billion dollars and took a decade to build must autonomously execute a sequence of events — heat shield deployment, parachute inflation, rocket ignition, cable deployment, touchdown — each one timed to the second, each one dependent on every step before it going exactly right. Miss any single step, or hit it five seconds too late, and the whole thing becomes a crater.
cur: 思考这个数字的含义。七分钟：从以每小时约20,000公里的速度首次接触大气到轮子着地、静止在另一个星球上。七分钟内，一艘耗资十亿美元、花费十年建造的航天器必须自主执行一系列事件——热盾展开、降落伞充气、火箭点火、缆索释放、着陆——每一个精确到秒，每一个都取决于之前的每一步都完全正确。错过任何单一步骤，或晚5秒执行，整个东西就会变成一个陨石坑。

en: And here is the detail that makes it genuinely terrifying: by the time Earth hears that the craft has touched the top of the Martian atmosphere, it has been on the ground — or part of the ground — for more than eleven minutes. The speed of light is not slow, but Mars is far enough that the round-trip lag runs anywhere from six to forty-four minutes depending on where the two planets are in their orbits. No one lands a Mars rover. No one on Earth can. The craft lands itself, in the dark, on the other side of the sun, and the people who built it can only sit in a room and wait to find out if it worked.
cur: 令人真正感到恐怖的细节是这样的：当地球听到航天器触及火星大气顶部的消息时，它已经在地面上——或者说在地面的一部分——超过11分钟了。光速并不慢，但火星的距离足够远，往返延迟根据两个行星在轨道上的位置而定，可以在6到44分钟之间。没有人在地球上操控火星漫游车。没有人能做到。航天器在黑暗中着陆，在太阳的另一侧，建造它的人只能坐在一个房间里，等待看看是否成功。

en: This is not a problem that gets easier with experience. Every world presents a different physics, a different atmosphere, a different set of constraints — and the solutions that worked on one body are useless, or dangerous, on another. The history of [entry, descent, and landing](/science/mission-phases/edl) is not a single story of improving technique. It is a collection of entirely different stories, each one a bespoke answer to the same brutal question: how do you slow down fast enough, without being crushed, in time, before you hit the ground?
cur: 这不是一个随着经验而变得更容易的问题。每个星球呈现出不同的物理，不同的大气，不同的约束条件——而在一个天体上奏效的解决方案在另一个天体上毫无用处，甚至很危险。[进入、下降和着陆](/science/mission-phases/edl)的历史不是一个关于改进技术的单一故事。它是完全不同故事的汇集，每一个都是对同一个残酷问题的定制答案：你如何在足够快的时间内减速足够多，而不被压碎，在你撞到地面之前？

en: Start with the easy case, which is not the Moon. The Moon has no atmosphere at all — which sounds like a gift, until you realize what an atmosphere is actually for. It is free deceleration. A spacecraft hitting the top of Earth's atmosphere at orbital velocity arrives with an enormous kinetic energy budget, and the air slowly burns it off: the heat shield glows, drag builds up, and a craft that was moving at kilometres per second bleeds off enough speed, over enough minutes, that a parachute can catch it. Take away the atmosphere and you take away all of that. On the Moon, you arrive fast and you have only rockets to slow you, so you must carry every kilogram of the propellant you need to kill that speed from the moment you leave Earth. The Apollo Lunar Module had a dedicated descent engine that burned for twelve minutes to bring two men down from orbit. Every kilogram of lander had to be earned in fuel on the launch pad. There is nothing free about landing on an airless world.
cur: 从简单的情况开始，那不是月球。月球根本没有大气——这听起来像是上天的馈赠，直到你意识到大气的真正用途。它是免费减速。以轨道速度撞击地球大气顶部的航天器携带着巨大的动能，空气慢慢地燃烧掉它：热盾发出光芒，阻力增加，一艘以每秒公里数运动的航天器在足够多的分钟里流失足够的速度，使得降落伞可以抓住它。取消大气，你就失去了所有这些。在月球上，你快速抵达，只能用火箭来减速，所以从离开地球的那刻起，你必须携带杀死那个速度所需的每一公斤推进剂。Apollo 月球舱有一个专门的下降引擎，燃烧12分钟，将两个人从轨道上降下来。每公斤的着陆器都必须在发射台上用燃料赚取。在无空气的世界上着陆没有任何免费的东西。

en: Mars is the cruel middle case, and it is the one that has killed the most missions. The Martian atmosphere exists — it is real carbon dioxide, roughly a hundred kilometres deep — but it is about one percent as dense as Earth's. Thick enough to matter, thin enough to be almost useless. A parachute that would stop a probe cold in Earth's air barely makes a dent in Mars; you need it, but you cannot rely on it. Every Mars lander to date has used an aeroshell — a blunt heat shield that creates drag while absorbing the thermal fury of entry — plus a supersonic parachute to pull the speed down further, and then something else on top of that, because the parachute alone never gets you all the way to safe.
cur: 火星是残酷的中间情况，也是杀死最多任务的那个。火星大气确实存在——它是真实的二氧化碳，大约100公里深——但它的密度大约是地球的1%。足够浓厚而有关系，足够稀薄而几乎无用。一个在地球大气中会立即停止探测器的降落伞在火星上几乎没有作用；你需要它，但你不能依赖它。迄今为止，每一个火星着陆器都使用了航天器壳——一个产生阻力同时吸收进入热核心的钝顶热盾——加上一个超音速降落伞来进一步降低速度，然后在上面还有其他东西，因为单独的降落伞永远无法让你达到安全状态。

en: That "something else" is the design problem. It is what makes every Mars landing different, and it is what every engineering team has had to solve from scratch. [Viking 1](/missions?id=viking1) solved it in 1976 the obvious way: retrorockets, fired during the final descent, slowing the lander to a gentle touchdown on Chryse Planitia — the first spacecraft ever to work on the Martian surface, and it ran for more than six years. The retrorocket approach is conservative and heavy; it works, but it demands fuel and it limits your mass budget for science. Twenty years later, [Mars Pathfinder](/missions?id=mars-pathfinder) tried something that sounds like a joke: wrap the entire lander in airbags, cut it loose at altitude, let the rockets fire upward to kill the last of the vertical speed, and then let it bounce. On July 4, 1997, the Pathfinder lander hit the surface of Mars at about 50 kilometres per hour and bounced at least fifteen times before rolling to a stop, whereupon the petals opened and [Sojourner](/missions?id=mars-pathfinder) — the first Mars rover — trundled out onto the rocks of Ares Vallis.
cur: 这个"别的东西"就是设计问题所在。正是它使得每次火星着陆都不同，也正是每支工程团队都必须从零开始解决的难题。[Viking 1](/missions?id=viking1)在1976年以最直接的方式解决了它：在最后的下降阶段启动制动火箭，将着陆器缓缓减速至克律塞平原的表面——这是第一艘在火星表面运作的航天器，它运行了超过六年。制动火箭方案保守且笨重；它能行，但需要消耗燃料，限制了你的科学载荷预算。二十年后，[Mars Pathfinder](/missions?id=mars-pathfinder)尝试了一个听起来像玩笑的方案：将整个着陆器包裹在充气气囊中，在高空释放，让火箭向上点火以消耗最后的垂直速度，然后让它反弹。1997年7月4日，Pathfinder着陆器以大约50公里/小时的速度撞击火星表面，弹跳了至少十五次后才停止滚动，随后花瓣打开，第一台火星漫游车[Sojourner](/missions?id=mars-pathfinder)就踏上了阿瑞斯谷的岩石。

en: Airbags work for small, light craft. Sojourner massed about 10 kilograms. By 2012, [Curiosity](/missions?id=curiosity) massed nearly 900. Airbags that could absorb that landing would weigh more than the rocket could afford to launch, so the team at JPL had to invent something new: the sky crane. The descent stage — a rocket-powered flying platform — carried the rover down on cables, matching the pace of the ground, and when the wheels touched the Martian surface the cables were cut and the descent stage flew off to crash-land at a safe distance. It is the most audacious landing sequence ever flown, and it worked perfectly on the first attempt, setting Curiosity down in Gale Crater at 2:32 in the morning, California time, on August 6, 2012.
cur: 气囊对小型、轻型航天器有效。Sojourner的质量约为10公斤。到2012年，[Curiosity](/missions?id=curiosity)的质量接近900公斤。能吸收这种着陆的气囊会重于火箭能承受的发射，所以JPL的团队必须发明新的东西：空中起重机。下降级——一个火箭动力飞行平台——通过缆索将漫游车运送到地面，匹配地面的速度，当车轮触及火星表面时缆索被切断，下降级飞离以安全距离硬着陆。这是有史以来飞行的最大胆的着陆序列，它在第一次尝试中完美奏效，在加州时间2012年8月6日凌晨2:32将Curiosity设置在盖尔撞击坑中。

en: The sky crane was not just an engineering novelty. It was a philosophical shift: instead of designing the lander to survive contact with the ground, the engineers separated the problem entirely — descent, then release, then ground contact — so that each piece could be optimized independently. [Perseverance](/missions?id=perseverance) used the same architecture on February 18, 2021, landing on the floor of [Jezero Crater](/mars) and then driving, over the following months, toward the ancient river delta on its northern rim. But Perseverance added one piece the sky crane had not carried: a system that looked at the ground and thought.
cur: 空中起重机不仅是一个工程新奇。它是一个哲学转变：与其设计着陆器以承受与地面的接触，工程师们完全分离了问题——下降、然后释放、然后地面接触——所以每一部分都能被独立优化。[Perseverance](/missions?id=perseverance)在2021年2月18日使用相同的架构，着陆在[耶泽罗撞击坑](/mars)的底部，然后在接下来的几个月驾驶，朝向其北缘的古老河流三角洲。但Perseverance增加了空中起重机没有携带的一件东西：一个看着地面并思考的系统。

en: Jezero is not a flat plain. It has steep cliffs, sand dunes, boulder fields, and smaller impact craters nested inside the rim — terrain that would have been considered unlanding-able under older rules. The reason Perseverance could target it was Terrain-Relative Navigation: a camera mounted on the belly of the descent stage photographed the surface rushing up, matched the image in real time against an onboard map of the crater, located itself to within metres, and then steered the vehicle away from hazards that the camera could see and the ground team could not respond to in time. The craft chose its own landing spot. The people who built it had given it the map and the authority; the decision, in those seven minutes, was entirely the machine's. The navigation essay's phrase for this comes from the landing side now, not the cruise: the craft learned to see — and then it used that sight to save itself.
cur: Jezero不是一个平坦的平原。它有陡峭的悬崖、沙丘、巨石田地，以及更小的撞击陨石坑在边缘内部嵌套——在旧的规则下会被认为是不可着陆的地形。Perseverance能够以它为目标的原因是Terrain-Relative Navigation：一个安装在下降级腹部的摄像机拍摄了冲上来的表面，实时将图像与陨石坑的车载地图相匹配，将自己定位到数米之内，然后将车辆转向摄像机可以看到但地面团队无法及时应对的危险。航天器选择了自己的着陆点。建造它的人给了它地图和权限；那七分钟中的决定完全是机器的。导航文章的短语现在从着陆方面而来，而不是巡航方面：航天器学会了看——然后它用那个视力来拯救自己。

en: Every world hands you a different problem. The Moon has no air, so you fall on rockets alone; Mars has just enough to cook you but not enough to catch you; Earth and Titan have enough that a parachute does most of the work. No arrival is ever quite the arrival before it.
cur: 每个星球都会给你一个不同的问题。月球没有空气，所以你只能靠火箭下落；火星有足够的空气来烹饪你但不足以抓住你；地球和土卫六有足够的降落伞完成大部分工作。没有到达曾经与之前的到达完全相同。

en: Mars at least gives you seven minutes. Venus gives you less time than that to do anything useful, and it will kill you no matter how well you land. The Soviet [Venera program](/missions?id=venera-13) is the story of engineers deliberately designing spacecraft to die gracefully — to survive long enough to return something before the planet destroyed them. When Venera 13 touched down on March 1, 1982, it had entered a 457-degree Celsius atmosphere pressing down at 89 times Earth's standard pressure — the equivalent of a kilometre of ocean water on every surface — and its engineers had expected it to operate for perhaps thirty-two minutes before the heat cooked the electronics. It lasted 127 minutes. In that time it drilled a soil sample, analysed it chemically, and transmitted two color panoramas of flat basaltic rock under an orange sky. Those images remain, today, the best photographs ever taken from the surface of Venus. No spacecraft has been back since.
cur: 火星至少给你七分钟。金星给你的时间少于这个来做任何有用的事，无论你着陆得多好，它都会杀死你。苏联的[Venera](/missions?id=venera-13)计划是工程师们故意设计航天器优雅地死亡的故事——生存足够长的时间以在星球摧毁它们之前返回一些东西。当Venera 13在1982年3月1日着陆时，它已经进入了457摄氏度的大气中，以地球标准大气压的89倍的压力向下压——相当于每个表面上有一公里的海水——它的工程师们期望它在热量烹饪电子之前运行大约32分钟。它持续了127分钟。在那段时间内，它钻取了土壤样品，在化学上进行了分析，并传输了两张平坦玄武岩在橙色天空下的彩色全景图。这些图像至今仍是从金星表面拍摄的最佳照片。此后没有航天器返回。

en: Descent through Venus's atmosphere is, at least, partly atmospheric: the thick CO₂ slows you. But there is no parachute phase that matters — the air is dense enough that even a relatively small drogue suffices to get you to terminal velocity, and after that the crushing pressure takes over. The engineering problem on Venus is not slowing down. It is surviving long enough to do anything after you stop.
cur: 通过金星大气的下降至少部分上是大气的：厚厚的CO₂使你减速。但没有降落伞阶段至关重要——空气的密度足够大，即使相对较小的引导伞也足以让你达到末速度，之后压力接管。金星上的工程问题不是减速。它是在停止后生存足够长的时间来做任何事情。

en: Titan, Saturn's largest moon, is the strangest case of all. [Huygens](/missions?id=cassini) — an ESA probe carried to the Saturn system aboard [Cassini](/missions?id=cassini) — was released on Christmas Day 2004 and fell for twenty-two days before hitting Titan's atmosphere on January 14, 2005. Titan's air is mostly nitrogen, denser than Earth's at the surface, and colder than minus 170 degrees Celsius — a thick, orange, hydrocarbon haze that scatters sunlight into permanent amber dusk. Huygens deployed its main parachute within four minutes of atmospheric contact, then switched to a smaller drogue about fifteen minutes into the descent to prevent the batteries from dying before it reached the surface. It fell for two hours and twenty-seven minutes — not seven minutes, but nearly two and a half hours — and when it finally touched a plain scattered with ice pebbles it was moving at about 4.5 metres per second, a pace a brisk walk would match. Then it sat on the surface and transmitted for another seventy-two minutes before Cassini carried out of view. Huygens remains the only spacecraft humanity has ever landed anywhere in the outer solar system. Nothing has gone back.
cur: 土卫六（土星的最大卫星）是最奇异的情况。[Huygens](/missions?id=cassini)——ESA的探测器，由[Cassini](/missions?id=cassini)携带进入土星系统——于2004年圣诞节发射，在坠落二十二天后于2005年1月14日进入土卫六大气层。土卫六的大气主要由氮气组成，比地表密度更大，温度低于零下170摄氏度——浓厚的橙色烃类烟雾将阳光散射成永久的琥珀色暮光。Huygens在接触大气后四分钟内展开主降落伞，随后在下降约十五分钟时切换到更小的尾伞，以防止电池在到达表面前耗尽。它下降了两小时二十七分钟——不是七分钟，而是几乎两个半小时——当它最终接触到散布着冰砾的平原时，速度约为每秒4.5米，相当于快速行走的步伐。随后它在表面坐了下来，又传输了七十二分钟，直到Cassini飞出视野。Huygens仍然是人类唯一在太阳系外部区域着陆过的航天器。没有其他的探测器再回过来。

en: Mars is the cruel middle case — too thin an atmosphere to parachute down, too thick to ignore. It all happens in about seven minutes: entry, peak heating, a supersonic parachute, heat-shield separation, powered descent, and a sky crane lowering the rover on cables. Every step must fire on its own, on time, or the mission ends in a crater.
cur: 火星是残酷的中间情况——大气太稀薄，无法靠降落伞着陆；但又太稠密，无法忽略。整个过程耗时约七分钟：进入、峰值加热、超音速降落伞、热盾分离、动力下降，以及天空起重机通过缆绳放下火星车。每一步都必须按时独立触发，否则任务会以坠入陨石坑而告终。

en: Perseverance hangs beneath its descent stage in the final seconds over Jezero Crater, moments before the sky crane pays out its cables — a manoeuvre flown entirely by the spacecraft itself, with Earth a spectator eleven minutes behind.
cur: Perseverance在耶泽罗撞击坑上方的最后时刻悬挂在下降级下方，距离天空起重机放出缆绳的时刻只有片刻——这个机动完全由航天器自主执行，地球只能在十一分钟后的观看。

en: Across the history of Mars missions specifically, the landing problem has a body count. Mars 2, in 1971, became the first object from Earth to touch the Martian surface — and crashed, killing itself on impact, the descent system having failed before the parachute sequence was complete. Mars Polar Lander, in December 1999, almost certainly shut down its descent engines prematurely when vibrations from the legs deploying were misread as a touchdown signal, and it fell the last forty metres at full speed. Beagle 2, on Christmas Day 2003, made it through entry — the EDL sequence appears to have worked — but the solar panels failed to fully deploy on landing and it could never communicate, silent on the Martian plains. The European Space Agency's Schiaparelli lander, in October 2016, had its inertial measurement unit saturate during the violent parachute descent — the readings briefly ran off the top of their scale — corrupting the navigation solution so the onboard computer believed it was already below the surface; it cut the parachute and fired the retrorockets for just three seconds instead of thirty, and hit the ground at roughly 540 kilometres per hour.
cur: 在火星任务的历史中，着陆问题是以生命为代价的。Mars 2在1971年成为首个触及火星表面的地球物体——但它坠毁了，在撞击中自毁，下降系统在降落伞序列完成之前便已失效。Mars Polar Lander在1999年12月，几乎可以肯定是因为着陆腿展开时的振动被误判为触地信号，而过早关闭了下降发动机，最后四十米它以全速坠落。Beagle 2在2003年圣诞节那天成功通过了进入阶段——EDL序列看起来运行正常——但太阳能电池板在着陆时未能完全展开，它再也无法通信，静静地躺在火星平原上。欧洲航天局的Schiaparelli着陆器在2016年10月，其惯性测量单元在剧烈的降落伞下降过程中饱和——读数瞬间超出了量程——导航解算因此被破坏，星上计算机错误地认为自己已经在地表以下；它抛掉了降落伞，只点燃了三秒而非三十秒的制动火箭，以大约每小时540公里的速度撞击地面。

en: Each failure is a different failure. That is the pattern. There is no single thing that kills Mars landers; there is a long list of single things, each one a different link in a sequence that has to hold. Every mission that has survived landing on Mars has done so by getting every step right, in order, autonomously, without a second chance. The sequence that [Curiosity](/missions?id=curiosity) and [Perseverance](/missions?id=perseverance) flew successfully is not simpler than the ones that killed their predecessors. It is, if anything, longer and more elaborate. What is different is the margin — the care with which each potential failure mode was identified, tested, and either fixed or designed around. The seven minutes that looked like terror from the outside were, from the inside, the seven minutes that the engineers had spent years making boring.
cur: 每一次失败都是不同的失败。这是模式。没有单一的东西会杀死火星着陆器；有的是一长串单一的东西，每一个都是序列中必须坚持的不同环节。每一个在火星上成功着陆的任务都是通过按顺序、自主地、不给第二次机会地做对每一步而做到的。[Curiosity](/missions?id=curiosity)和[Perseverance](/missions?id=perseverance)成功飞行的序列并不比杀死其前驱的序列更简单。如果有什么的话，它更长更精细。不同之处在于余量——每一个潜在的失效模式被识别、测试、修复或绕过的谨慎程度。从外部看起来像恐怖的七分钟，从内部看，是工程师们花了多年时间使其变得乏味的七分钟。

en: Schiaparelli was meant to prove Europe could land on Mars. In 2016 its computer, briefly confused by its own sensors, decided it had already touched down — let go of its parachute, cut its thrusters, and fell the last kilometres. The record of arrivals is written as much in craters as in triumphs.
cur: Schiaparelli本应证明欧洲能在火星上着陆。2016年，其计算机短暂地被自己的传感器所迷惑，误以为已经接触到地面——松开了降落伞，切断了推进器，从最后的数公里高度坠下。到达的记录就像写在胜利中一样，也写在陨石坑中。

en: Here is what makes this different from almost every other engineering problem: you cannot test it. You can test the parachute in a wind tunnel, the sky crane on a cable rig, the heat shield in an arc-jet facility — but you cannot test the full sequence, at full scale, in the actual atmosphere of Mars. Every Mars landing is a first flight of the complete system. Every EDL team in history has sent their machine off with a set of simulations, a set of engineering tests, a model of the atmosphere they are about to enter, and then waited. The Martian atmosphere is not uniform; its density varies with season and dust loading in ways that the models approximate but do not perfectly capture. A parachute deploying into slightly thinner air than expected needs to open a few seconds sooner; a lander touching down on a slope rather than a flat plain needs a slightly different retrorocket sequence. The software bakes in these contingencies, but the atmosphere gets a vote.
cur: 正是这一点使其与几乎所有其他工程问题不同：你无法测试它。你可以在风洞中测试降落伞，在缆绳钻机上测试天空起重机，在电弧喷气设施中测试热盾——但你无法测试完整的序列，以完整的规模，在火星的实际大气中。每一次火星着陆都是完整系统的首飞。每一个EDL团队在历史上都曾用一套模拟、一套工程测试、一个他们即将进入的大气模型来发送他们的机器，然后等待。火星大气并不均匀；其密度随季节和尘埃负荷而变化，方式是模型近似但并不完美捕捉的。展开到比预期略稀薄空气中的降落伞需要提前几秒打开；着陆在斜坡而非平原上的着陆器需要略微不同的制动火箭序列。软件将这些应急措施烘入其中，但大气有发言权。

en: This is, in a specific sense, the thing navigation never has to face. [Navigation](/essays/navigation) is an iterative business — you aim, check, correct, aim again, for months or years, each correction building on the last. EDL is a one-shot event. The trajectory corrections have been made; the orbit has been shaped; the approach has been dialled in with millimetric care. Then the aeroshell hits the atmosphere and the countdown begins, and every decision from that moment is made by the machine, running code written years earlier by engineers who are now sitting in a room in Pasadena, watching a number on a screen that tells them only whether the signal is still there.
cur: 从特定意义上说，这是导航永远不必面对的事情。[导航](/essays/navigation)是一项迭代业务——你瞄准、检查、纠正、再瞄准，持续数月或数年，每次纠正都建立在前一次的基础上。EDL是一次性事件。轨迹修正已经完成；轨道已经塑形；进近已经以毫米级的精度进行了调整。随后气动壳进入大气，倒计时开始，从那一刻起的每一个决定都由机器做出，运行由多年前在Pasadena一个房间里工作的工程师编写的代码，他们现在正坐在那里，看着屏幕上的一个数字，它只告诉他们信号是否仍在。

en: When that signal disappears — as it always does, for those long minutes while the aeroshell is a fireball — the room goes quiet. Not because they don't know what's happening. They have the timeline memorized. They know, to the second, when parachute deployment should occur, when the heat shield should separate, when the sky crane should ignite. They count through it, together, in silence, watching a clock. And when the signal comes back and says *I am on the ground*, what you hear from that room is not a sentence. It is a sound that has no words in it, because there are no words adequate for a machine the size of a car landing itself safely on another planet, alone, while the people who built it were standing eleven light-minutes away, unable to help.
cur: 当那个信号消失时——对于那些长时间的气动壳是火球的时刻，它总是会消失——房间陷入寂静。不是因为他们不知道发生了什么。他们已经把时间表背得烂熟。他们精确地知道降落伞应该何时展开、热盾应该何时分离、天空起重机应该何时点火。他们一起数着时间，沉默地，看着一个时钟。当信号回来说*我在地面*时，你从那个房间听到的不是一个句子。它是一个没有文字的声音，因为没有足够的文字来描述一个汽车大小的机器在另一个星球上安全地自己着陆，孤独地着陆，而建造它的人们站在十一光分之外，无法帮助。

en: And you cannot help it through any of it. Mars is light-minutes away — the whole descent fits inside the radio lag. By the time the first word of entry reaches Earth, the craft is already down, safe or dead, the outcome decided minutes before anyone here knew it had begun.
cur: 而且你无法在任何时候帮助它。火星距离是光分——整个下降过程都在无线电延迟范围内。当进入的第一个字到达地球时，航天器已经着陆了，安全或已死，结果在任何人这里知道它已经开始前数分钟就已经决定了。

en: Every world is different. The Moon demands rocket fuel for every metre per second of descent. Mars demands aerodynamics, parachutes, rockets, and then — because the parachute gets you only partway — invention. Venus demands thermal armor and a ticking clock. Titan offered the unexpected gift of a thick atmosphere and used it to give Huygens two and a half hours of descent data from the outer solar system, the most distant landing in history, still unmatched. Each solution is shaped by the planet that forced it into existence, and none of them transfers cleanly to the next body down the list.
cur: 每个世界都不同。月球要求每米每秒下降的火箭燃料。火星要求空气动力学、降落伞、火箭，然后——因为降落伞只能带你到一半——发明。金星要求热装甲和滴答的时钟。土卫六提供了浓厚大气的意外礼物，用它给Huygens二个半小时的太阳系外部下降数据，这是历史上最远的着陆，仍未被超越。每一个解决方案都由迫使其存在的行星塑造，其中没有一个能够干净地转移到列表中的下一个天体。

en: What they share is this: the moment of landing is the moment when everything that cannot be undone happens. The months of cruise, the years of trajectory refinement, the decades of engineering — all of it has been moving toward a window of a few minutes during which the machine either does the thing or it doesn't, and there is no one close enough to intervene. The [navigation problem](/essays/navigation) has been solved, in pieces, over seventy years, by iterating: aim, correct, aim, correct. The landing problem must be solved in advance, completely, and then trusted. You cannot correct a Mars landing in progress. You can only watch the clock and count the beats of a sequence you no longer control, and wait for the signal that tells you the machine did what you asked.
cur: 它们的共同点是：着陆时刻是无法撤销的一切发生的时刻。数月的巡航、数年的轨迹改进、数十年的工程——所有这一切都在朝着一个几分钟的窗口移动，在这个窗口中机器要么做这个事，要么不做，而且没有人离得足够近以至于能够干预。[导航问题](/essays/navigation)已经通过迭代在七十年间得到了分段解决：瞄准、纠正、瞄准、纠正。着陆问题必须提前完全解决，然后被信任。你不能在火星着陆进行中进行纠正。你只能看着时钟，数着一个你不再控制的序列的跳动，等待信号告诉你机器完成了你要求的事情。

en: Perseverance is on the floor of [Jezero Crater](/mars) right now, picking its way toward ancient geology that may or may not hold what we sent it there to find. Viking 1's bones are still on Chryse Planitia. Huygens sits on a plain of ice pebbles more than a billion kilometres away. [Venera 13](/missions?id=venera-13) lasted 127 minutes and went silent. Each of them got down by solving a different problem, with a different answer, in a different set of minutes that could not be re-run. The cruise is easy. The physics carry you. Arriving is where the work is — and every world makes you invent the work from scratch.
cur: Perseverance现在在[耶泽罗撞击坑](/mars)的底部，向我们派它去寻找的可能也可能不包含的古代地质特征缓慢移动。Viking 1的残骸仍然在克律塞平原上。Huygens坐在十亿多公里外的冰砾平原上。[Venera 13](/missions?id=venera-13)持续了127分钟然后沉默了。他们每一个都通过解决不同的问题、用不同的答案、在无法重新进行的不同时间段内着陆的。巡航很容易。物理学会推动你。到达才是工作所在——每个世界都让你从零开始发明工作。

en: The Deep Space Network was built for a handful of probes. It is about to face the traffic of a solar-system civilisation. The fixes — antenna arrays, laser links, a store-and-forward internet — are real, and they are already being built. None of them beats the speed of light.
cur: 深空网络建立之初是为了服务少数几个探测器。如今它即将面对太阳系文明时代的通信流量。解决方案——天线阵列、激光链路、存储转发式互联网——都是现实的，并且已在建设中。但没有任何一种能够超越光速。

en: The [comms essay](/essays/comms) ended on a quiet note: three patches of desert, roughly forty antennas, a 22-watt whisper crossing billions of kilometres, and the recognition that this threadbare infrastructure carries everything humanity has ever learned about the outer solar system. The miracle, that essay argued, wasn't how much the Deep Space Network had lost — it was how little. Three sites, one frequency band per mission, a schedule overbooked by forty percent, an upgrade programme running five years late. By any engineering standard, the [DSN](/science/mission-phases/dsn) should have broken under the load years ago. It hasn't, mainly because the load has grown slowly enough, and the engineers patient enough, that the cracks could be papered over one antenna track at a time.
cur: [通信论文](/essays/comms)以一个宁静的音符结尾：三片沙漠、大约四十根天线、一声22瓦的耳语穿越数十亿公里，以及对一项事实的认知——这套简陋的基础设施承载了人类对外太阳系所了解的一切。那篇论文论证的奇迹不在于Deep Space Network丢失了多少，而在于它丢失了多少。三个站点、每个任务一个频段、时间表超订40%、升级计划晚了五年。按照任何工程标准衡量，[DSN](/science/mission-phases/dsn)本应在多年前就在负荷下崩溃。它没有，主要是因为负荷增长得足够慢，工程师足够耐心，裂缝可以一根天线轨道地被修补起来。

en: That arithmetic is about to stop working. The 2020s and 2030s are set to deliver a wave of missions — crewed Artemis flights with their appetite for continuous high-rate data, science probes to the ice giants, commercial operators who have been promised DSN time without anyone fully accounting for where it will come from, and eventually a sustained human presence on the Moon that will require something closer to a broadband connection than a telex line. NASA's own projections, published in successive DSN strategic reviews, show demand growing by a factor of ten before 2035. The current infrastructure was not designed to absorb a factor of ten. The bottleneck, it turns out, has never been the spacecraft. It has always been the ground.
cur: 这种算术即将失效。2020年代和2030年代将带来一波任务——载人的Artemis飞行任务及其对连续高速率数据的胃口、前往冰巨星的科学探测器、被承诺了DSN时间的商业运营商（尽管没人完全考虑过这时间从何而来），以及最终月球上持续的人类活动，需要的不是电传打字机线路而是更接近宽带连接的东西。NASA自身的预测，发表在历次DSN战略评估中，显示到2035年前需求将增长十倍。现有基础设施并非为吸收十倍增长而设计。事实证明，瓶颈从来不在航天器。它一直在地面。

en: Three approaches are being built in parallel. Stop building bigger dishes and instead combine many smaller ones in software — arraying. Replace radio with laser light for the high-rate downlinks, which concentrates orders of magnitude more data into the same transmitted power. And accept that the solar system will never have a real-time network, building instead an architecture designed for that fact: a store-and-forward internet whose packets spend hours in transit and arrive anyway. Each has been demonstrated. None of them changes the one thing that cannot be changed.
cur: 三种方法正在并行建设中。不再建造更大的天线盘，而是在软件中联合许多较小的天线——阵列化。将高速率下链的无线电替换为激光，将数个数量级的数据集中到相同的传输功率中。并接受太阳系永远不会有实时网络的事实，改为构建一个为此事实而设计的架构：一个存储转发式互联网，其数据包需要数小时才能到达，但最终还是会送达。每种方法都已被演示。没有一种能改变唯一无法改变的东西。

en: The [comms essay](/essays/comms) worked through the link budget: [Voyager 1](/missions?id=voyager-1)'s 22.4-watt transmitter, the inverse-square loss across tens of light-hours, the femtowatt signal arriving at a 70-metre dish after more than twenty-three light-hours of travel. That loss is real, and it is why data rates from the outer planets are measured in bits per second. But it is not the binding constraint for the missions launching right now. At the Moon and Mars, spacecraft can transmit faster than the ground can schedule time to receive. The DSN allocates antenna time in blocks called tracks — typically eight to ten hours per mission per day — fought over by a queue of dozens of active spacecraft. [MAVEN](/missions?id=maven), the Mars atmospheric orbiter that relays data for surface missions, can generate and forward data faster than the DSN can absorb it on any given day. The spacecraft is not the problem. The three sites, with their fixed number of dishes and finite receiver chains, are the problem. The traditional answer was to build a bigger dish: the 70-metre giants at each complex were expanded from 64 metres specifically to support [Voyager 2](/missions?id=voyager-2)'s Neptune encounter in 1989 — a civilisational upgrade to the global network, for one flyby, of one planet. That kind of expenditure is not repeatable, and a 70-metre dish is near the practical limit of what can be steered as a single structure anyway. The era of the bigger dish is over.
cur: [通信论文](/essays/comms)详细分析了链路预算：[Voyager 1](/missions?id=voyager-1)的22.4瓦发射机、跨越数十光小时的平方反比衰减、信号经过二十三小时多的旅途后以飞瓦计的强度到达一个70米的天线盘。这种衰减是真实的，这就是为什么来自外行星的数据速率以比特每秒为单位。但这不是当前发射任务的制约因素。在月球和火星上，航天器的传输速度超过了地面安排接收的时间。DSN以称为轨道的时段分配天线时间——通常每个任务每天八到十小时——由几十个活跃航天器的队列争夺。[MAVEN](/missions?id=maven)，这个火星大气轨道器为地表任务中继数据，产生和转发数据的速度超过了DSN在任何一天能吸收的量。航天器不是问题。三个站点，拥有固定数量的天线盘和有限的接收链，才是问题。传统答案是建造一个更大的天线盘：每个综合体的70米巨型天线从64米扩建而来，特别是为了支持[Voyager 2](/missions?id=voyager-2)1989年的海王星遭遇——对全球网络的一次文明级别的升级，为了一次飞掠，一个行星。这种支出规模是无法重复的，而且70米天线盘已接近可作为单一结构转向的实际极限。更大天线盘的时代已经结束。

en: The principle behind [antenna arraying](/science/mission-phases/antenna-arrays) is straightforward, though the engineering is not. Take a signal arriving simultaneously at multiple separate antennas. Combine their outputs — accounting precisely for the tiny difference in arrival time at each dish, caused by their different positions on the ground — and the combined system behaves like a single dish whose collecting area is the sum of all the individual dishes. Eight 34-metre antennas combined coherently produce roughly the sensitivity of a single 96-metre dish, which is larger than anything the DSN has ever built. The signal-to-noise ratio improves as the square root of the number of antennas; the cost of each additional dish is a fraction of the cost of upgrading the primary to match the same gain.
cur: [天线阵列化](/science/mission-phases/antenna-arrays)的原理很直接，尽管工程并不简单。取同时到达多个独立天线的信号。联合它们的输出——精确地考虑由于天线在地面上的不同位置而导致的到达时间的微小差异——联合系统的表现就像单个天线，其采集面积是所有单个天线的总和。八个34米天线相干地联合产生大约96米单个天线的灵敏度，这比DSN建造过的任何东西都大。信噪比随天线数量的平方根而改善；每增加一个天线盘的成本是升级主天线盘以达到相同增益成本的一小部分。
